title: ggwas: Modern GWAS Visualizations
text: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) generate large amounts summary statistics require effective visualization interpretation publication. standard tools R (qqman, CMplot) rely base R graphics offer limited customization. Modern genomics workflows benefit plotting system integrates ggplot2. allows layered customization, journal-specific theming, composition multi-panel figures. ggwas designed three goals: Broad coverage: 21 plot types one package, including views found GWAS plotting packages. Publication-ready defaults: sensible colors, proper axis formatting, built-journal themes plots look good without tweaking. Performance scale: smart downsampling handles 10M+ variant datasets without manual intervention. package reads output PLINK, REGENIE, GCTA, GEMMA, generic tab-separated file. plot functions return standard ggplot objects, can add layers, override themes, combine panels patchwork exactly ggplot.

text: Manhattan plot common GWAS visualization. point tested variant, plotted genomic position (x) association strength -log10(p-value) (y). Chromosomes alternate color visual separation. interpret: Look “towers” points rising genome-wide significance line (red dashed, p = 5×10⁻⁸). tower locus evidence true association. Isolated points line worth investigating may artifacts. broad signal spanning multiple chromosomes equally (rather discrete peaks) can indicate unresolved population stratification. Check QQ plot case.  Label strongest signals switch different palette:
code: manhattan_plot(example_gwas) manhattan_plot(   example_gwas,   label_top_n = 5,   colors = gwas_palette("vibrant") )

title: ggwas: Modern GWAS Visualizations
text: datasets extreme p-values (e.g. biobank GWAS), small p-values always imply large, robust effects: rare alleles perfect case/control assortment can produce astronomical p-values despite negligible unreplicable effects. y_metric = "beta_min" plots lower bound effect-size confidence interval: |beta| - 2*SE. Variants whose CI overlaps zero excluded, revealing large, robust effects:  Many hits visible standard plot disappear effect-confidence view large SE makes confidence interval overlap zero, hallmark artifacts rare variants.
code: set.seed(42) n <- 5000 sim <- data.frame(   CHR = sample(1:22, n, replace = TRUE),   BP = sample(1:250e6, n),   SNP = paste0("rs", seq_len(n)),   P = runif(n)^3,   BETA = rnorm(n, 0, 0.02),   SE = abs(rnorm(n, 0.03, 0.005)) ) real <- sample(n, 15) sim$P[real] <- 10^(-runif(15, 5, 12)) sim$BETA[real] <- rnorm(15, 0, 0.5) sim$SE[real] <- runif(15, 0.01, 0.03) fake <- sample(setdiff(seq_len(n), real), 10) sim$P[fake] <- 10^(-runif(10, 8, 15)) sim$BETA[fake] <- rnorm(10, 0, 0.05) sim$SE[fake] <- runif(10, 0.08, 0.2)  sim_gwas <- as_gwas_data(sim)  library(patchwork) p1 <- manhattan_plot(sim_gwas) + ggtitle("Standard: -log10(p)") p2 <- manhattan_plot(sim_gwas, y_metric = "beta_min", label_top_n = 3) +   ggtitle("Effect confidence: |beta| - 2*SE") p1 / p2

title: ggwas: Modern GWAS Visualizations
text: identifying GWAS locus, fine-mapping narrows variant likely causal. Tools like SuSiE FINEMAP assign variant posterior inclusion probability (PIP, 0–1) group high-PIP variants credible sets. interpret: Large points high PIP strong causal candidates. Color indicates credible set membership: variants set LD statistically distinguished. locus one large red point (PIP > 0.8) well-resolved; locus many medium-sized points one set residual uncertainty. Multiple credible sets one locus suggest independent signals:
code: fm_data <- example_gwas fm_data$PIP <- runif(nrow(fm_data))^5 fm_data$PIP[which.min(fm_data$P)] <- 0.92 fm_data$PIP[order(fm_data$P)[2:3]] <- c(0.65, 0.4) fm_data$credible_set <- NA_integer_ fm_data$credible_set[fm_data$PIP > 0.05] <- 1L  finemapping_plot(   fm_data,   region = "chr1:1000000-50000000",   label_pip_above = 0.3 )

title: ggwas: Modern GWAS Visualizations
text: Genetic correlation (rg) measures much genetic basis two traits overlaps. ranges -1 (perfectly opposing genetic effects) 0 (independent) +1 (shared genetic architecture). LDSC GREML estimate rg GWAS summary statistics alone, without individual-level data. interpret: Red cells indicate traits share risk variants (e.g., BMI T2D). Blue cells indicate opposing genetics (e.g., height T2D). Clustering reveals groups genetically related traits. Stars mark statistically significant correlations. figure essential understanding trait relationships cross-trait genomics:  Alternative palette without clustering:
code: traits <- c("BMI", "Height", "WHR", "T2D", "CAD", "SBP", "HDL") set.seed(123) rg <- matrix(0, 7, 7, dimnames = list(traits, traits)) rg[lower.tri(rg)] <- runif(21, -0.6, 0.8) rg <- rg + t(rg) diag(rg) <- 1  genetic_correlation(rg, show_values = TRUE, palette = "RdBu") genetic_correlation(rg, show_values = TRUE, palette = "PRGn", cluster = FALSE)

title: ggwas: Modern GWAS Visualizations
text: large datasets (common imputed GWAS 10-40M variants), ggwas applies smart downsampling default. algorithm preserves significant near-significant variants spatially binning dense cloud non-significant points. resulting plot visually indistinguishable plotting points, renders seconds rather minutes:
code: manhattan_plot(large_gwas)                        # auto (target: 200k points) manhattan_plot(large_gwas, downsample = FALSE)    # all points (slow) manhattan_plot(large_gwas, downsample_n = 500000) # custom target

title: ggwas: Modern GWAS Visualizations
text: Since every ggwas function returns standard ggplot object, can compose multi-panel figures using patchwork way ggplot:
code: library(patchwork)  p1 <- manhattan_plot(example_gwas, label_top_n = 3) +   labs(tag = "A") + theme_nature() p2 <- qq_plot(example_gwas) +   labs(tag = "B") + theme_nature() p3 <- volcano_plot(example_gwas, label_top_n = 5) +   labs(tag = "C") + theme_nature()  p1 / (p2 | p3) + plot_layout(heights = c(2, 1))

text: data gwas_data object data.frame GWAS results. chr, bp, p, snp Column name overrides (auto-detected NULL). colors Two-color vector alternating chromosomes. point_size Point size. alpha Point transparency. genome_wide Genome-wide significance threshold (p-value). suggestive Suggestive significance threshold. threshold_colors Colors significance lines. highlight_snps Character vector SNP IDs highlight. highlight_color Color highlighted SNPs. highlight_size Size highlighted points. label_snps Character vector SNP IDs label. label_top_n Label top N significant SNPs. label_column Column use label text. downsample Enable smart downsampling large datasets. downsample_n Target number points downsampling. chromosomes Subset chromosomes plot (integer vector). chr_labels Custom chromosome labels.
